title: Wolf and Sigil
premise: Hazel Voss, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has hidden his magic for a decade in a city where spells are punishable by death, selling harmless charms to survive. When a mute child arrives speaking the First Tongue — the language that binds oaths into flesh — Hazel learns the child is a living sigil, and that King Aldric has been hollowed out and worn like armor by the Oath-Eater, an ancient hunger that devours sworn words. To save both king and city, Hazel must speak his forbidden true oath aloud, sacrificing the identity he built in exile; the child, revealed as the remnant of Aldric's stolen self, must choose whether to return to the man or remain free. In the end Hazel unbinds the king at the cost of his own oath-name, becoming no one — and finding, for the first time, someone.
about_author: I. M. Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing medieval oath documents before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about the weight of promises, and live quietly with two dogs who have never once kept a secret.

chapters.title: The Child Who Spoke First
chapters.summary: POV: Hazel. In the rain-slicked charm market of Greyhollow, Hazel's careful anonymity shatters when a barefoot boy appears at his door, speaking words that make Hazel's dormant oath-scar burn. The boy cannot lie, cannot age, and calls Hazel by a name he buried ten years ago. Emotional beat: dread blooming into reluctant recognition — the past has found him.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: POV: Hazel, with interludes from the child. Fleeing the Wardens, Hazel uncovers the truth: King Aldric made an unbreakable oath years ago, and something ancient has been feeding on it ever since, wearing him from the inside. The child is the piece of Aldric the thing couldn't digest. Emotional beat: guilt — Hazel's own broken oath a decade ago opened the door.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Hazel and the child. Hazel infiltrates the palace during the Oathfeast, where every citizen renews loyalty vows that feed the Eater. He confronts the hollowed king and begins the counter-oath, but it requires a speaker's true name freely given — and the child offers himself instead. Climax: Hazel refuses the sacrifice and speaks his own name into the binding. Emotional beat: love choosing truth over survival.

chapters.title: No One, Someone
chapters.summary: POV: Hazel, then briefly the restored king. The Eater starves and unravels; Aldric wakes in his own body, mortal and diminished, while Hazel's oath-name burns away, leaving him free of the order that bound him — and unknown even to himself. The child chooses freedom over reunion, staying at Hazel's side. Resolution: identity rebuilt not from duty, but from chosen bonds. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace.
